items.answer: Immersion is the objective, quantifiable degree to which a virtual reality system projects stimuli onto the sensory receptors of users in an extensive, matching, surrounding, vivid, interactive, and plot-informing way.

Immersive technology is a technology that produces an experience in which a person perceives an environment through sensory organs as real, so that they cannot distinguish it from their real environment.

An immersive experience is a perceived experience through sensory organs that appears real, because a person cannot distinguish the experienced environment from their real environment and perceives it as that real environment.

Metaverse is a broad view of an all-around three-dimensional environment in which people act as in the real world through natural interaction with digital content, reimagining human interaction with the digital world rather than being merely an application of virtual reality, mixed reality, or augmented reality technology.

Virtual reality (VR) is an artificial environment experienced through sensory stimuli provided by a computer, in which a person's actions partially determine what happens and which replaces the user's sense of reality without requiring the physical existence of objects or places.

questions.question: When is the early era placed in the historical evolution of virtual reality?
options: During the popularity of virtual reality
Before the advent of digital computers
During the growth of consumer virtual reality
After the advent of digital computers
questions.explanation: The early era is the phase that existed before digital computers appeared, while the later phases unfold after that point. The popularity of the term and the growth of consumer hardware belong to later phases, not the early era.

data.text: Virtual reality's historical evolution is broadly divided into four mostly distinct, sometimes overlapping phases. They form a timeline from the early era before digital computers, through the formative years and the modern phase, to the current growth phase. The approximate spans are before digital computers, roughly 1950 to 1990, 1991 to 2015, and roughly 2016 onward.
points: Virtual reality's evolution has four mostly distinct, sometimes overlapping phases: before digital computers, roughly 1950-1990, 1991-2015, and roughly 2016 onward.

questions.question: Which immersion principle is anticipated by early stereoscopic demonstrations?
options: Flat images can be perceived as a three-dimensional environment
Several recorded senses can be replayed together as one experience
Artificial objects can form a non-real environment
Head motion can be tracked to change a viewpoint
questions.explanation: Early stereoscopic demonstrations showed that the brain can treat two-dimensional images as three-dimensional objects and space, which is the visual basis of VR immersion. Tracking, replayed senses, and fully artificial environments belong to later or different developments.

questions.question: What role does a later stereoscope play in the pre-computer history of depth perception?
options: It was a head-tracked display and a step toward computer-generated scene experiences
It was a multi-sensor simulator and a step toward controlled flight experiences
It was a sensory replay device and a step toward recorded multi-sensory experiences
It was a compact display and a step toward practical immersive experiences
questions.explanation: A later stereoscope was a compact-sized stereoscopic display that advanced the earlier stereoscopic demonstration and is roughly considered another step toward practical immersive experiences. It is not defined by flight sensors, head tracking, or replayed multi-sensory stimuli.

questions.question: Why is an early flight simulator treated as a precursor to modern immersive virtual reality?
options: It evolved into multi-sensor immersive experiences
It evolved into compact stereoscopic immersive experiences
It evolved into head-tracked computer-generated immersive experiences
It evolved into recorded multi-sensory immersive experiences
questions.explanation: The early flight-simulator development evolved into sophisticated flight simulators with multiple sensors that provide an immersive experience, making it a precursor to modern multi-sensory immersive VR. It is not defined by replayed recorded senses, head-tracked computer-generated scenes, or compact stereoscopic displays.

data.text: Before digital computers appeared in the 1940s, a few developments already anticipated immersive virtual reality. Stereoscopic devices showed that the brain can perceive 2D images as 3D objects and space, the display principle later used in virtual reality. Brewster’s later stereoscope made that depth effect more practical, while Link’s flight simulator concept extended immersion through multiple sensors.
points: The early pre-computer era before 1940s digital computers included a few key developments conceptually similar to immersive virtual reality.
Wheatstone’s 1838 stereoscopic device first showed the brain can perceive 2D images as 3D, the principle VR uses for immersion.
Brewster’s 1860 compact stereoscope improved Wheatstone’s device, making stereoscopic depth a more practical step toward immersive experience.
Edwin A. Link’s 1928 flight simulator concept evolved into multi-sensor simulators, a precursor to modern multi-sensory immersive virtual reality.

questions.question: What made Sensorama count as an immersive virtual reality system under the modern definition?
options: Screen-based force feedback
Data-glove input support
Head-tracked computer-generated graphics
Pre-recorded multi-sensory stimulation
questions.explanation: Sensorama counted as immersive because it stimulated several sensory organs with pre-recorded effects. Head-tracked graphics, screen-based force feedback, and data-glove input were associated with other developments, not with what made Sensorama immersive.

questions.question: What distinguished Sutherland's Sword of Damocles from the earlier Philco head-mounted display?
options: It demonstrated pre-recorded smells and wind in an immersive vehicle
It demonstrated head tracking together with computer-generated imagery
It demonstrated force feedback while manipulating objects on a screen
It demonstrated motion tracking in a bulky, uncomfortable wearable display
questions.explanation: The Philco display could track motion but was bulky and uncomfortable, while Sutherland's system was significant for combining head tracking with computer-generated imagery. The other options describe different developments: Sensorama's sensory effects and Brooks's haptic feedback.

questions.question: What role did the term artificial reality play in the history of immersive technologies?
options: It was a name for a force-feedback device used with computer screens
It was the term proposed for immersive technologies in the late 1980s
It was the name of a commercially available stereoscopic head-tracked display
It was an early term that evolved into virtual reality
questions.explanation: Artificial reality was an earlier label that later developed into the term virtual reality, rather than being the late-1980s term itself. It was not the name of a specific display or haptic device.

questions.question: How did the early force-feedback system increase the sense of touch in a screen-based experience?
options: It let a user feel on-screen objects while manipulating them
It let a user operate a data glove as a haptic input device
It let a user track head motion in a bulky head-mounted display
It let a user see a wide field of view on a regular monitor
questions.explanation: The force-feedback system added touch by letting users feel the on-screen objects they were manipulating. It did not provide head tracking, wide-field monitor display, or data-glove haptics.

data.text: The formative history of virtual reality covers its second historical phase, from roughly 1950 to 1990. It begins with head-mounted displays, then introduces immersive and haptic systems that broadened what users could experience. Later terminology, commercial head-mounted displays, and public presentations helped shape the field's modern name and visibility.
points: Virtual reality's formative years were its second phase, roughly 1950 to 1990, from early HMDs to the term virtual reality.
Early head-mounted displays led to Sutherland's first 1967 head-tracked, computer-generated HMD, the Sword of Damocles.
Heilig's Sensorama was the first immersive virtual reality system, stimulating vision, sound, smell, wind, and haptics.
Brooks's 1967 haptic feedback system let users feel objects on a screen while manipulating them.
The term changed from artificial reality to Lanier's virtual reality, while commercial HMDs and public papers also appeared.

questions.question: What made a CAVE an immersive virtual reality display?
options: It combined stereo sound with a single flat monitor
It replaced the user's vision with a head-mounted display
It presented a virtual scene on a screen in front of the user
It surrounded the user with computer-rendered images
questions.explanation: A CAVE was immersive because it rendered a surrounding virtual setting around the user, not because it was a head-worn device or a single screen.

questions.question: What role did WTK and VRML serve in the development of virtual reality systems?
options: They gave hardware makers a standard way to attach head tracking
They gave developers higher-level tools for building applications
They gave users cheaper head-mounted displays for home use
They gave display rooms a larger surrounding field of view
questions.explanation: WTK and VRML were software and modeling approaches that supported application development, not hardware-standardization or display-size improvements.

questions.question: What long-term trend did head-mounted displays show from the late 1950s through the modern phase?
options: They became more expensive and less practical over time
They became more dependent on surrounding projections over time
They became less bulky and more usable over time
They became limited to a fixed field of view over time
questions.explanation: HMDs evolved from bulky early models toward lighter, more portable, and more usable forms. They did not become dependent on room-scale projections or uniformly less practical.

questions.question: What followed from the availability of inexpensive VR headsets?
options: Greater interest in VR modeling languages towards the end of the modern phase
Greater interest in surrounding display rooms towards the end of the modern phase
Greater interest in early HMD prototypes towards the end of the modern phase
Greater interest in virtual reality towards the end of the modern phase
questions.explanation: Inexpensive headsets made VR more accessible and helped spur broader interest in virtual reality itself, rather than specifically driving interest in CAVE-style rooms, modeling languages, or early prototypes.

data.text: VR's modern phase, roughly 1990 to 2015, is traced through developments that expanded how virtual environments could be created and experienced. Early advances included immersive CAVE displays and software tools for building VR applications. Later HMD improvements made headsets more practical, and the inexpensive Oculus Rift helped make VR affordable and increased interest near the phase's end.
points: The modern phase of virtual reality (VR) spanned roughly 1990 to 2015.
The CAVE used one Silicon Graphics computer to make users feel surrounded by immersive holograms.
Sense8's WTK package and modeling languages such as VRML, X3D, and Java 3D helped build VR systems.
The White 5 HMD had a 150-degree field of view, while HMDs became more portable, less bulky, and more usable.
Palmer Luckey's inexpensive Oculus Rift, bought by Facebook, made VR affordable and spurred interest late in VR's modern phase.

questions.question: What started the growth phase of VR?
options: Commercial headsets from well-known companies made immersive VR affordable for many people
Inexpensive headsets from small startups made immersive VR affordable for many people
Research headsets from academic labs made immersive VR affordable for many people
Immersive displays from research groups made immersive VR affordable for many people
questions.explanation: VR's growth phase began when well-known companies released commercial headsets that made immersive VR affordable to a large population. Smaller-startup, lab, or research-group hardware did not cause the phase to begin.

questions.question: What best explains the renewed public interest in the term Metaverse?
options: Popularization by the research community made people take it up and interpret it differently
Popularization by Zuckerberg of Meta made people take it up and interpret it differently
Popularization by Apple's VR headset made people take it up and interpret it differently
Popularization by early VR software made people take it up and interpret it differently
questions.explanation: The Metaverse term existed earlier but gained public attention after Zuckerberg of Meta popularized it, leading people to take interest and interpret it in different ways. Earlier use in the research community did not create that renewed interest.

questions.question: Why is the VR growth phase described as continuing?
options: Competition among headset makers will push further development of headsets, displays, and input devices
Huge demand will push further development of headsets, displays, and input devices
Research interest in the Metaverse will push further development of headsets, displays, and input devices
Standardized virtual environments will push further development of headsets, displays, and input devices
questions.explanation: The growth phase is continuing because ongoing demand is expected to drive better headsets, immersive displays, and input devices. Other factors may affect the field, but the continuing phase is tied to this demand-driven development.

data.text: VR's growth phase began around 2016 as commercial headsets from major companies made immersive experiences affordable to many. During this continuing phase, Zuckerberg of Meta popularized the older Metaverse term in 2021, increasing interest and activity, and Apple released the Apple Vision Pro in 2023. Huge demand may accelerate better headsets, immersive displays, and input devices, so the growth phase is expected to continue.
points: Commercial VR headsets from major companies, released around 2016, made immersive experiences affordable to many, starting VR's growth phase.
Zuckerberg of Meta popularized the 1990s Metaverse term in 2021, sparking broader interest and activity.
Apple released the Apple Vision Pro virtual reality headset in 2023.
VR's growth phase continues because huge demand may accelerate developments such as better headsets, displays, and input devices.

questions.question: What subject does the available online book by LaValle cover in detail?
options: The historical evolution of augmented reality
The development of virtual environments
The historical evolution of virtual reality
The use of virtual reality in healthcare
questions.explanation: LaValle's online book provides a detailed account of the historical evolution of virtual reality, not of augmented reality history or of specific virtual reality applications.

data.text: LaValle's book is available online. It covers the historical evolution of virtual reality in detail. This gives learners a complete reference for VR history.
points: The online book by LaValle covers the historical evolution of virtual reality in detail.

questions.question: Why can Sir Charles Wheatstone's 1838 stereoscopic device be regarded as a first step toward virtual reality?
questions.reference_answer: It established that the human brain can process two-dimensional images as three-dimensional objects. In virtual reality, headsets present two-dimensional images, and stereoscopic vision makes the user perceive them as three-dimensional objects and space, which is immersion. The device is therefore roughly considered a first step toward immersive experience.

questions.question: Why is Morton Heilig's Sensorama considered an early immersive virtual reality system rather than only a visual display?
questions.reference_answer: Sensorama can be considered the first immersive virtual reality system under the modern definition of virtual reality. It was publicized as having 3D, wide vision, motion, color, stereo sound, smell, wind, and vibrations, and it stimulated all sensory organs by letting a user feel pre-recorded vibrations, sounds, smells, and wind. Therefore it was more than a visual display.

questions.question: Why is Sutherland's Sword of Damocles an important milestone in the development of virtual reality head-mounted displays?
questions.reference_answer: It was the first demonstrated head-mounted display that combined head tracking with computer-generated imagery. This showed that a headset could follow the user's motion and present computer-generated content. Later head-mounted displays evolved from such early systems into more portable and usable forms.

questions.question: How did the 2016 commercial virtual reality headset releases extend the effect that inexpensive headsets had already had near the end of the modern phase?
questions.reference_answer: Near the end of the modern phase, the availability of inexpensive headsets, such as the Oculus Rift, greatly spurred interest in virtual reality. In 2016, many well-known companies released commercial virtual reality headsets, making immersive experiences affordable to a large population and spurring growth. This began the current growth phase.
